Clio Coder 0.3.0 is the first release you can install from npm, and the first
one we are putting in front of the general public. It is a terminal coding
agent for people who work on real scientific and HPC codebases, built on one
bet: you should not have to hand a remote model a shell to get useful agentic
coding. You bring the model, local llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang,
a cloud API, a ChatGPT or Claude subscription, or an ALCF inference gateway,
and Clio brings the harness: twenty typed tools behind one admission path, a
fleet of bounded workers that runs across your cluster over SSH, and an
integrity-sealed receipt for every run.

```bash
npm install -g @iowarp/clio-coder
clio-coder configure
```

This is a soft beta of experimental software. Interfaces may break between
minor versions. Use version control, review proposed changes, and keep backups
when operating on repositories you care about.

## Highlights

- **One namespace, first publish.** Everything the tool writes on your machine
  now lives under `clio-coder`: the binary, the XDG config/data/state/cache
  directories, the `.clio-coder/` project directory, the generated
  `CLIO-CODER.md` handbook, and `CLIO_CODER_*` environment variables. Future
  CLIO ecosystem tools (clio-core, clio-agent, clio-kit) coexist without
  collisions. There are no migration shims: 0.3.0 is the baseline.
- **The agent ledger.** Concurrent workers in one dispatch now share a bounded
  coordination board. A worker posts typed entries: a claim that stakes a path
  scope so peers stop duplicating work, a cited finding a peer can corroborate,
  or a review of another entry. The orchestrator is the sole writer and stamps
  every attribution, so a worker cannot forge authorship; findings render as
  corroborated, uncorroborated, or an ungrounded lead, and never collapse into
  a consensus that could bury the single dissenting worker who found the real
  bug. Every run's receipt seals its ledger contribution.
- **Compete mode candidates that actually disagree.** `mode: "compete"` now
  assigns each candidate a distinct engineering stance (minimal diff,
  test-first, refactor-tolerant, spec-literal), and the judge reports where the
  candidates diverged, not just which one won.
- **The soak: a benchmark whose subject is Clio, not the model.** A weak model
  that never repairs the fixture passes because the machinery behaved; a strong
  model fails the moment Clio breaks a promise about itself: an unsealed
  receipt, an unauthenticated seal, a republished transcript. It runs offline
  against a local target, because a gate on Clio's own invariants that needs a
  cloud key is not a gate.
- **Fleet contracts grew teeth.** Per-step write allowlists verified by
  diffing against a pinned baseline with rollback of unauthorized changes,
  bounded check/repair loops compiled into one deterministic hashed DAG,
  deterministic `code` steps that run registry-owned commands rather than
  model-authored shell strings, and durable capacity leases that survive
  process death.
- **Token accounting that refuses to lie.** Usage is observed from the live
  stream, never assumed; a runner that saw no usage reports unmeasured rather
  than zero; thresholds on unmeasured metrics fail closed. Receipt-derived
  accounting covers surfaces that publish no usage stream.
- **Safety hardening.** Damage-control matching now evaluates commands that
  will execute rather than prose a file happens to contain; provider URLs open
  through `spawn()` instead of a shell; retries stop after a failed attempt has
  executed a potentially state-changing tool; ACP deadlines are mandatory
  schedulable bounds.
- **Headless continuity and a saner help surface.** `clio-coder run --session`
  and `--continue` append to real session history or exit before any model
  call, and the default `--help` shows the surface a person needs while
  `--help --all` keeps the full harness for scripts and agents.

The full changelog entry for 0.3.0 in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-coder/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
carries the complete list with the reasoning behind each change.

## If you used a pre-release build

0.3.0 reads only the `clio-coder` namespaces. Reconfigure your targets,
reinstall project skills (`clio-coder skills install <name> --force`), and
remove stale `clio` launchers from earlier source installs. Old `clio`
namespace directories are ignored and can be deleted.

## The ecosystem

Clio Coder is the interactive coding agent in [IOWarp](https://iowarp.ai)'s
CLIO ecosystem of agentic science, built by the
[Gnosis Research Center](https://grc.iit.edu) at Illinois Tech with the
University of Utah. [clio-kit](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-kit) contributes
MCP servers for HDF5, Slurm, ParaView, Pandas, NetCDF, FITS, Zarr, and ArXiv;
[clio-core](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core) is the tiered context-storage
layer underneath. Funded by the National Science Foundation under
[Award #2411318](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2411318).

Docs: [github.com/iowarp/clio-coder/tree/main/docs](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-coder/tree/main/docs).
Security reports: [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-coder/blob/main/SECURITY.md), never public issues.

Built for the people who maintain the code that science runs on.
